title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In 'Algèbre des figures', L is an ambient space, most likely PL or polyhedral given the use of interiors and closures. A figure F in L is a finite set of closed 'pieces' A. Their open parts A° are pairwise disjoint and cover the support |F|. The pieces are ordered by inclusion (the face order), and each piece is the union of the open parts of the pieces below it. On p.26 Grothendieck compares three order relations on figures: ≤, ≪ (refinement/subdivision) and ≼. On p.28 he concludes that he has built an infimum F.G of F and G for ≪.

Struck-out first attempt (top of p.27). Given figures F and G, set K = {(A,B) ∈ F×G | A°∩B° ≠ ∅}. Then:
- |F|∩|G| is the disjoint union of the sets A°∩B° for (A,B) ∈ K.
- These sets are the classes of the equivalence relation on |F|∩|G| generated by R_F and R_G. More precisely, it is the common refinement: the intersection of the two relations, called a 'borne sup' in the 'finer = larger' ordering.
- The pieces of the new figure should be C_k = A∩B for k = (A,B).

Rewritten version. A figure is recoded as a surjection φ: S → I from a subset S ⊂ L onto a finite ordered set I. The closed pieces are A_i = φ^{-1}(I_{≤i}) and the open strata are A_i° = φ^{-1}(i). Given a second figure φ': T → I', consider ψ = (φ,φ'): S∩T → I×I'. Its image J = K = {(i,i') | A_i°∩A'_{i'}° ≠ ∅} carries the order induced from the product and has projections J → I and J → I'. For j = (i,i') one gets the boxed formula A_j = ψ^{-1}(J_{≤j}) = A_i ∩ A'_{i'}.

This gives the 'intersection figure' F.G with |F.G| = |F|∩|G|. The next page extends it to arbitrary families (|∧F_i| = ∩|F_i|) and stresses that F.G must not be confused with the naive intersection F∩G inside P(L), except when F and G are compatible. In modern terms, a figure is a finite poset-stratified subspace (a map to a poset whose closed strata are the preimages of down-sets). F.G is the product stratification restricted to S∩T, re-indexed by the image poset. This is the meet for refinement.
errors: The boxed identity ψ^{-1}(J_{≤(i,i')}) = A_i∩A'_{i'} is purely formal: x lies in A_i∩A'_{i'} iff φ(x)≤i and φ'(x)≤i'. What is not formal is whether the resulting pieces satisfy the figure axioms. One needs the closure of A_i°∩A'_{i'}° to equal A_i∩A'_{i'}, and the product order on J to be the face/closure order. This holds for convex polyhedra when the relative interiors meet (Rockafellar, Thm 6.5). It can fail for general closed pieces, where A∩B may be strictly larger than the closure of A°∩B°. The page does not address this; it presumably relies on the polyhedral axioms of the 'contexte' (C5–C8).
Notational slip: the target is written I×J, but the description {(i,i') ∈ I×I'} shows it should be I×I'. The intermediate poset J is itself the image K.

The struck-out draft speaks of 'borne sup' of the equivalence relations R_F and R_G. As relations under inclusion, the correct operation is the intersection (meet); 'sup' is only right in the 'finer is bigger' convention.

ideas.what: Encoding a figure (finite stratification) as a surjection φ: S → I onto a finite ordered set, with closed pieces φ^{-1}(I_{≤i}) and open strata φ^{-1}(i)
ideas.modern_name: poset-stratified space (continuous map to a poset with the Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Treumann, 'Exit paths and constructible stacks' (2009); Lurie, Higher Algebra, Appendix A; later Ayala–Francis–Tanaka. The idea is implicit in earlier stratification theory.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses tame topology and stratified structures, but not this poset-map formalism as far as I know

ideas.what: Intersection figure F.G as the image of S∩T → I×I', giving the meet of two figures for refinement, with |F.G| = |F|∩|G| and pieces A_i∩A'_{i'}
ideas.modern_name: common refinement / product (intersection) stratification; meet of decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (common refinement of cell decompositions, polyhedral complexes, o-minimal cell decompositions)

ideas.what: Partition of |F|∩|G| into the sets A°∩B° as the common refinement of the two equivalence relations

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck formalizes figures (stratified subspaces) as surjections onto ordered sets, with closed pieces given by preimages of down-sets. He constructs intersections via the product poset. This is essentially the poset-stratified-space formalism that became standard only around 2009 (Treumann, Lurie). It is an early instance of that viewpoint inside his tame-topology program.
missed.quote: S ↓φ surj I ... I, J ens. ord. ... K = Im(S∩T →(φ,φ') I×J) ... A_j = A_i ∩ A'_{i'}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical rather than technical. It documents that Grothendieck's 'algèbre des figures' (tame topology after the Esquisse) used the poset-map description of stratifications. That links his program to modern exit-path and constructible-sheaf theory. The mathematical content itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine common-refinement construction. The only mildly notable point is the early, clean poset-surjection encoding of stratifications in an unpublished tame-topology manuscript.
transcription_corrections: The second ambient subset is written S' (with a mark) in the first diagram and T in the second; both denote the same second support set.

In the bottom line, the definitions are meant to read A_i = φ^{-1}(I_{≤i}) and A'_{i'} (written A'_j) = φ'^{-1}(I'_{≤i'}). The transcription's 'A_i' = φ^{-1}(I_{≤i})' and 'A_j = φ^{-1}(I_{≤j})' garble the primes.
In the second diagram the map ψ goes from S∩T down to the (script) J, with arrows J → I and J → I'. The label 'I, J ens. ord.' probably means I, I' (the index posets).
In the struck-out passage, 'les relations A°∩B°' is likely 'les parties A°∩B°' (the parts), described as the classes of the equivalence relation on |F|∩|G|.
